text:
Asha (People Ops): Quick heads-up — rolling out two policy updates that go into effect 2026-04-15. TL;DR: 1) Emergency Caregiver Leave (ECL): up to 5 paid days in a rolling 12-month window for urgent caregiving (child, elder, immediate-family medical emergencies, court/placement). 2) Volunteer Time Off (VTO): 16 paid hours/year (1.33 hrs/month), for company-recognized volunteer activities. Full details + examples in the HR page: https://intranet.redwood.example/hr/policies/ecl-vto (doc updated). Please read and share with your teams.
Asha (People Ops): Key notes: ECL is separate from PTO and short-term disability, doesn't affect accruals, and can be taken in half-day increments. Managers approve in HiBob within 48 hours; retrospective approvals allowed for emergencies. VTO must be scheduled/approved by your manager; no cash-out and non-transferable.
Priya (People Ops): Adding that ECL can be used for urgent adoption/foster placement day-of needs and travel to arrange emergency care. We'll flag any patterns for follow-up with managers to provide support — not to penalize.
Liam (Finance): Question: how will ECL affect payroll/tax reporting? Do we roll into regular payroll or record separately for reporting?
Devon (Legal): ECL is paid leave — treated like regular wages for tax purposes. We'll keep a separate ECL code for reporting so People Ops and Finance can track utilization trends (code: ECL_PAY). No impact on benefits eligibility.
Asha (People Ops): Good call — Finance, we'll share the ECL payroll code and a one-page ops checklist by Friday. Also increasing emergency travel reimbursement cap for immediate-family emergencies to $2,000 per incident (was $1,000). Receipts required; pre-approval required for anything > $500.
Liam (Finance): Got it — we'll update expense policy and reimbursement workflows. Can People Ops confirm whether corporate cards can be used for these bookings? That affects accounting flow.
Priya (People Ops): Corporate card OK for travel when available. If not, submit through the expense form with the ECL incident tag. We'll provide a short Concur/expense example in the FAQ.
Devon (Legal): Small compliance note — international travel reimbursements still subject to local tax rules. We'll draft a short blurb per region and attach it to the policy doc.
Engineer (someone in thread): Quick question — can ECL be used for school emergency events (kid sent home sick)?
Asha (People Ops): Yes — immediate caregiver needs like child sent home sick qualify. Use ECL for same-day care; if you expect it will extend, coordinate PTO or an unpaid option with your manager.
Priya (People Ops): Manager guidance: approve within 48 hours where possible; if a manager is unavailable, escalate to the manager's manager or People Ops for faster approval.
Liam (Finance): Implementation note: we'll create a new payroll code and map it to the ECL_hours category starting next pay period after 2026-04-15.
Devon (Legal): Also adding a brief Code of Conduct reminder in the doc about respectful handling of leave requests and confidentiality of medical info.
people-ops-bot: Policy doc updated: "Emergency Caregiver Leave & Volunteer Time Off (ECL + VTO)" — https://intranet.redwood.example/hr/policies/ecl-vto (effective 2026-04-15) :sparkles:
Asha (People Ops): We'll run a brief manager training drop-in next week (two 30-min sessions) to walk through the approval flows and examples. Sign-ups will be posted in #people-ops. Thanks everyone. :heart:
Priya (People Ops): FAQ highlights will follow — how to request, examples of qualifying events, expense tagging, and manager checklist.
Liam (Finance): I'll coordinate the payroll mapping with HRIS and send confirmation once done.
Devon (Legal): I'll add the regional tax blurb and ensure the wording avoids creating unintended contractual obligations.
Engineer: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
Asha (People Ops): If you have urgent questions before the doc goes live, DM me or ping #people-ops.
